from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The 'Why': Explicit vs. Implicit", [
            "We know functions like y equals x squared.",
            "Some curves, like circles, trap y inside.",
            "Implicit differentiation lets us find their slope."
        ])
        
        # Animation Elements
        explicit_text = Text("Explicit: y = f(x)", color=WHITE)
        implicit_text = Text("Implicit: F(x, y) = 0", color="#FFD700")
        diff_text = Text("Differentiate y with respect to x", color=WHITE)
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=72, color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(explicit_text, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(explicit_text))
        self.play(explicit_text.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(implicit_text, 'E2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(implicit_text))
        self.play(implicit_text.animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(explicit_text), FadeOut(implicit_text))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.place_at_grid(diff_text, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(question_mark, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(diff_text), Write(question_mark))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Core", [
            "Recall the chain rule for derivatives.",
            "Treat y as a function of x.",
            "Always multiply by dy/dx when differentiating y."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        chain_rule = MathTex(
            r"\frac{d}{dx} [f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) \cdot g'(x)",
            font_size=36
        )
        self.place_at_grid(chain_rule, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(chain_rule))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight components
        f_g_x = chain_rule[0][12:18] # f'(g(x))
        g_x = chain_rule[0][19:22]  # g'(x)
        
        self.play(
            f_g_x.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            g_x.animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        box = SurroundingRectangle(chain_rule, color="#FF00FF", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Step-by-Step Algorithm", [
            "Step 1: Differentiate both sides regarding x.",
            "Step 2: Collect all dy/dx terms together.",
            "Step 3: Factor out and solve for dy/dx."
        ])
        
        equation = MathTex("x^3 + y^3 = 6xy", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "B2")
        self.add(equation)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        step1_eq = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}(x^3 + y^3) = \frac{d}{dx}(6xy)", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(step1_eq, "C3")
        self.play(Write(step1_eq))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        step2_eq = MathTex(r"3x^2 + 3y^2 \frac{dy}{dx} = 6y + 6x \frac{dy}{dx}", font_size=32)
        step2_grouped = MathTex(r"(3y^2 - 6x) \frac{dy}{dx} = 6y - 3x^2", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(step2_eq, "D3")
        self.play(Write(step2_eq))
        self.wait(1)
        self.place_at_grid(step2_grouped, "E3")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(step2_eq, step2_grouped))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        result = MathTex(r"\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{6y - 3x^2}{3y^2 - 6x}", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(result, "F3")
        self.play(Write(result))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Geometry of a Bouncing Ball", 
                          ["We apply this to complex paths.", 
                           "Find tangent slopes for any point.", 
                           "Easily determine velocity on any curve."])
        
        # --- Elements ---
        equation = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 = r^2", color="#FFFFFF")
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#00FF00")
        ball = Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.15)
        tangent_line = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color="#FFD700")
        
        # Initial positions
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # --- Animation ---
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.add(ball)
        ball.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(self.time * 2)))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(tangent_line, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(tangent_line)
        
        def update_tangent(mob):
            angle = self.time * 2
            point = circle.point_at_angle(angle)
            mob.move_to(point)
            # Tangent is perpendicular to radius vector (angle + PI/2)
            mob.set_angle(angle + PI/2)
        
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Cleanup
        ball.remove_updater(None)
        tangent_line.remove_updater(None)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Quick Check", [
            "Chain rule is key for implicit differentiation.",
            "Remember to always include dy/dx.",
            "Verify every y term derivative carefully."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        title = Text("Summary: Implicit Differentiate", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(title, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        checklist = VGroup(
            Text("1. Differentiate", color="#00FFFF"),
            Text("2. Group dy/dx", color="#00FFFF"),
            Text("3. Solve for dy/dx", color="#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        success = Text("SUCCESS!", color="#00FF00", font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(success, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(success.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(success.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(success))

        self.wait(2)

sections.title: The 'Why': Explicit vs. Implicit
sections.content: Briefly review explicit functions (y = f(x)) where y is isolated. Introduce the limitation: many curves (like circles or hearts) cannot be written as a single function of y. Use an animation showing a circle x² + y² = r² and explaining we need a way to find the slope (dy/dx) even when y is 'trapped'.
sections.example: Comparing y = x² (Easy) vs. x² + y² = 25 (The 'trapped' y).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Core
sections.content: Recall the Chain Rule: d/dx [f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x). Emphasize that whenever we differentiate a term containing 'y' with respect to 'x', we must treat 'y' as an inner function and multiply by dy/dx.
sections.example: Visualizing d/dx [y²] as 2y * (dy/dx) using a 'shadow' operator metaphor.

sections.title: The Step-by-Step Algorithm
sections.content: Present the 3-step process: 1. Differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to x. 2. Group all dy/dx terms on one side. 3. Factor out dy/dx and solve. Use a 'Robot Assembly Line' animation to show terms being processed.
sections.example: Differentiating x³ + y³ = 6xy (The Folium of Descartes).

sections.title: Application: The Geometry of a Bouncing Ball
sections.content: Demonstrate the power of the technique. Find the slope of the tangent line to a complex path at a specific point. This shows the practical utility of finding velocity/slope when a coordinate is defined implicitly.
sections.example: A cat running along a figure-eight path: finding the exact direction the cat is heading at a specific coordinate.

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check
sections.content: Review the 'Chain Rule' requirement. Provide a final 'Don't Forget' tip: Always verify that the dy/dx is present whenever a 'y' term is differentiated. Flash a summary slide.
sections.example: Quick fire: What is d/dx [sin(y)]? Answer: cos(y) * dy/dx.
